summary: Defines the Relay Agent Subscriber-ID option for DHCPv6. It lets a relay agent associate a stable subscriber identifier with client messages, independent of the client hardware and the physical network. It is a standards-track document.

eli5.summary: The network keeps a name tag for each customer's account that stays the same even if they get a new computer or plug into a different socket.

questions: what does a dhcpv6 relay agent do
subtitle: A DHCPv6 option that lets a relay agent tag client messages with a stable subscriber identity.

tldr.problem: Service providers want to tie a customer's DHCPv6 configuration to the customer's administrative information, independent of the client and of the physical network the customer connects through.
tldr.mechanism: A new Relay Agent Subscriber-ID option (code 38) lets a relay agent add a provider-assigned subscriber-id to relayed client messages. Its format is not standardized.
tldr.outcome: The server can use the subscriber-id, along with other data, to choose addresses, prefixes and configuration without being reconfigured when the subscriber moves.

today: RFC 4580 is a Proposed Standard and the unit metadata shows no RFC obsoleting or updating it.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
DHCPv6 (RFC 3315) provides IP addresses and configuration information for IPv6 clients. It includes a relay agent capability: processes within the network infrastructure receive multicast messages from clients and relay them to DHCPv6 servers. A relay agent may add information to a message before relaying it.

The information relay agents supply can also feed the server's decisions about the addresses, delegated prefixes and configuration parameters a client receives.
sections.eli5: A relay agent is a helper who passes a customer's request along to the office that hands out settings, and can scribble a note on it first.

sections.title: Why a Subscriber-ID
sections.content:
In complex service provider environments there is a need to connect a customer's DHCPv6 configuration with the customer's administrative information. The subscriber-id carries a value that can be independent of the physical network configuration through which the subscriber is connected. It complements, and might be used with, network-based information.

The provider-assigned value is intended to stay stable as customers connect through different paths and as the network changes. It lets the provider assign or activate subscriber-specific actions, such as specific IP addresses, prefixes, DNS configuration or accounting. A subscriber moving from one access point to another would not need reconfiguration at the provider's DHCPv6 servers.
sections.eli5: It is like a library card number. Whichever branch you walk into, the number says who you are.

sections.title: The Option Format
sections.content:
The option has a 2-byte option code, a 2-byte length and then the subscriber-id data. The option code is OPTION_SUBSCRIBER_ID (38). The option-len field is the length in octets of the subscriber-id field, with a minimum of 1 octet.

The subscriber-id is only for use within a single administrative domain and is only exchanged between relay agents and DHCPv6 servers in that domain. So its format and encoding are not standardized, and the RFC sets no semantic requirements on the data. Because the DHCPv4 Subscriber-ID suboption (RFC 3993) uses NVT ASCII data, using that encoding may be beneficial where both DHCPv4 and DHCPv6 are in use.
sections.eli5: The tag is a label saying what kind of note it is, how long it is, and then the note. What the note says is up to each company.

sections.title: Relay Agent Behavior
sections.content: DHCPv6 relay agents may be configured to include a Subscriber-ID option in relayed RELAY-FORW messages. How the subscriber-id is assigned, and the mechanisms used to configure it, are outside the scope of the RFC.
sections.eli5: The helper can stick the name tag on the request before passing it on. How it learns the name is not covered here.

sections.title: Server Behavior
sections.content:
The option gives the DHCPv6 server additional information. The server may use it, if available, together with other relay agent option data, options in the client messages and physical network topology information, to assign IP addresses, delegate prefixes and other configuration parameters. There is no special additional processing for the option.

A server is not required to return the option and its data in a RELAY-REPLY message.
sections.eli5: The office can read the name tag as one more clue when deciding what settings to give. It does not have to copy the tag back.

sections.title: Security and IANA
sections.content:
The option is only exchanged between relay agents and DHCPv6 servers. RFC 3315, Section 21.1 gives details on securing DHCPv6 messages sent between servers and relay agents, and Section 23 gives general DHCPv6 security considerations.

IANA has assigned DHCPv6 option code 38 for the Relay Agent Subscriber-ID Option.
sections.eli5: Because the tag only travels between the helper and the office, the existing rules for protecting that link cover it.

fields.name: option-len
fields.desc: Length in octets of the subscriber-id field; minimum 1.
